title: Data import: allow alternative match keys per row (e.g. credit code, else country + registration no.)
body:
## Context

In hotsrm a supplier's identity depends on where it is registered (ADR-0007): domestic suppliers are unique by `credit_code`, overseas ones by `country + registration_no` (`credit_code` is blank for them). One legacy supplier sheet contains both.

## Gap

`ImportRequest.matchFields` is a single key set for the whole import. With `matchFields: ['credit_code']`, overseas rows have a blank key and `upsert` creates them again on every run (duplicates), unless `skipBlankMatchKey` is set, in which case they are not imported at all.

## Proposal

Accept an ordered list of key sets, first non-blank one wins per row:

```json
{ "writeMode": "upsert", "matchKeys": [["credit_code"], ["country", "registration_no"]] }
```

(or `matchFields` accepting `string[][]`). Ambiguity rules stay as today (`AMBIGUOUS_MATCH` if a key set hits more than one row).

## Workaround in hotsrm (temporary)

Import the same sheet twice with `skipBlankMatchKey: true`: pass 1 `matchFields: ['credit_code']`, pass 2 `matchFields: ['country', 'registration_no']`. Each pass skips the other kind of row. Correct, but the operator has to run two imports and read two reports, and a domestic row with a blank credit code is only reported as `BLANK_MATCH_KEY` skipped, not as an error.

Linked: objectstack-ai/hotsrm#10
